blocks.text: Human skeletal system consists of 206 bones. Skeleton has two main divisions i.e., axial skeleton and appendicular skeleton (Fig. 12.5).

blocks.alt: A front view of the whole skeleton inside a body outline; axial bones in blue and appendicular bones in pink. Axial labels on the right: Cranium and Facial bones (Skull), Middle ear Ossicles, Neck bone (Hyoid), Chest bone (Sternum), Ribs, Vertebral column. Appendicular labels on the left: Pectoral girdle, Humerus, Ulna, Radius, Pelvic girdle, Carpals, Metacarpals, Phalanges, Femur, Patella, Tibia, Fibula, Tarsals, Metatarsals, Phalanges.
blocks.caption: Figure 12.5: Human skeleton (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 12.5).

blocks.text: The axial skeleton forms the axis of the body. Its bones support and protect the organs of the head, neck, and chest. It consists of skull, ribs, spine, and sternum.
a- Skull: It consists of the following 22 bones.

items: Eight cranial bones form cranium (brain box). The 2 paired bones are parietal bones and temporal bone. The 4 unpaired bones are frontal bone, occipital bone, ethmoid bone, and sphenoid bone.

Fourteen facial bones are attached to the cranium. The 6 paired bones are lacrimal, zygomatic, nasal bones, inferior nasal concha, maxilla and palatine. The 2 unpaired bones are mandible (jaw bone) and vomer.

blocks.alt: Two views of the skull with each bone in its own colour. Lateral view: Frontal, Parietal (2), Temporal (2), Occipital, Sphenoid, Ethmoid, Nasal (2), Lacrimal (2), Zygomatic (2), Maxilla (2) and Mandible, the mandible hinged at the temporal bone. Front view to mention the facial bones: Nasal (2), Lacrimal (2), Inferior nasal concha (2), Maxilla (2), Mandible, Palatine (2), Zygomatic (2) and Vomer.
blocks.caption: Figure 12.6: Human skull (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 12.6).

blocks.text: b- Middle ear: There are 6 bones (3 pairs) in middle ears. These are called ossicles and include malleus, incus and stapes.

blocks.alt: A section through the ear with brackets for the external ear, middle ear and internal ear. The ear canal ends at the eardrum; the malleus touches the eardrum, the incus lies between, and the stapes footplate sits in the oval window of the internal ear. An arrow leads to an enlarged view of the three ossicles: Malleus, Incus, Stapes.
blocks.caption: Figure 12.7: Middle ear ossicles (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 12.7).

blocks.text: c- Neck bone: Hyoid bone is a small single bone which lies at the base of skull below the tongue. It does not articulate with any other bone of head.
d- Vertebral column: It consists of 33 bones called vertebrae. The vertebrae make five groups:

items: Seven cervical vertebrae: These are the vertebrae of the neck. The first one is called atlas and the second one is called axis.
Twelve thoracic vertebrae: These are rib-carrying vertebrae and are found in chest region.
Five lumbar vertebrae; These are present in abdominal region.
Five sacral vertebrae; These are five fused vertebrae forming the sacrum. The sacrum articulates with the iliac bones of the hip to form the back of the pelvis.
Four coccygeal vertebrae or coccyx; these vertebrae are fused in the adults. Sacral and coccygeal vertebrae are together called pelvic vertebrae.

blocks.text: e- Rib Cage & Chest bone: The rib cage consists of 24 bones (12 pairs) called ribs and a sternum. The sternum (chest bone) is a long flat bone located in the central part of the chest. The ribs articulate posteriorly with the thoracic vertebrae. On anterior side, 7 pairs of ribs attach directly with the sternum by means of separate costal cartilages. These are called true ribs. The 8th, 9th and 10th pairs attach to the sternum by means of a common costal cartilage and are called false ribs. The last 2 pairs of ribs (11th and 12th) are known as floating ribs, because they do not attach to the sternum.

blocks.alt: A side view of a body outline with the head and brain, and inside it the S-curved vertebral column, each region in its own colour and bracketed: Cervical (7), Thoracic (12), Lumbar (5), Sacral (5 fused) and Coccygeal (4 fused). The first two vertebrae are labelled Atlas and Axis; an intervertebral disc lies between the bodies, and the spinal cord runs from the brain down behind them.
blocks.caption: Figure 12.8: Vertebral column (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 12.8).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed Figure 12.8 labels read 'Lumber' and 'Spinal chord'. The correct terms are lumbar (vertebrae) and spinal cord, as drawn above.

blocks.alt: A front view of the rib cage: twelve pairs of ribs numbered 1 to 12 from the thoracic vertebrae, the sternum in the middle and costal cartilage joining the ribs to it. Ribs 1 to 7 are true ribs, joined to the sternum by their own cartilage; ribs 8 to 10 are false ribs, joined through the cartilage of rib 7; ribs 11 and 12 are floating ribs with free front ends.
blocks.caption: Figure 12.9: Rib cage (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 12.9).

blocks.text: Appendicular skeleton includes the bones present in appendages (arms and legs). These are pectoral girdle, pelvic girdle, forelimbs and hindlimbs.

a- Pectoral girdle: It consists of 2 pairs i.e., a pair of clavicles (collar bones) and a pair of scapulae (shoulder bones). One end of each clavicle articulates with the sternum. The other end articulates with the scapula.
b- Forelimbs: Each forelimb (arm, wrist, hand, fingers) consists of the following 30 bones.

items: One humerus: It is a long bone, the end of which has a spherical head, which fits into the glenoid cavity.
One ulna and one radius: These are long bones. Ulna is on the inner side of arm while radius is on outer side (thumb side). Ulna is slightly bigger than radius.
Eight carpels: There short bones present in two rows and form the wrist. The upper row articulates with the radius and forms the wrist joint.
Five metacarpals: These bones make up the palm of the hand.
Fourteen phalanges: Each finger has 3 phalanges while the thumb has 2 phalanges.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints “Eight carpels”. The eight wrist bones are the carpals; carpels are parts of a flower.

c- Pelvic girdle: It is made up of two hip bones. Each hip bone contains 3 bones i.e., ileum, ischium and pubis. In each hip bone, there is a bony socket, called acetabulum that is composed of the fusion of three bones. The two hip bones are joined at the front by the pubic symphysis (a cartilaginous joint that connects the pubic bones at the midline of the body).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints “ileum” as a bone of the hip. The hip bone is made of the ilium, ischium and pubis; the ileum is the last part of the small intestine.
d- Hindlimbs: Each hindlimb (leg, ankle, foot, toes) consists of 30 bones.

items: One femur: It is a long thigh bone. Its head fits into the acetabulum of pelvic girdle.
One patella or kneecap: It is embedded in a long tendon which runs over the knee joint.
One tibia and one fibula: Tibia or shin bone is the large bone in the leg. Fibula or outer bone is a thin bone that joins the tibia just below the knee joint and just above the ankle.
Seven tarsals: These are short bones which are tightly attached to form the ankle.
Five metatarsals: These bones articulate with the tarsal and phalanges to form the sole of the foot.
Fourteen phalanges: Each toe has 3 phalanges while the big toe comprises 2 phalanges.
